describe("P-4 and P-11 — amounts are hidden; identities, timing and frequency are not", () => {
  // ⚠ **The first form of this test FAILED ON THE NEGATIONS** — *"No key source
  // hides identities"* matched, because the guard looked for `not` and the
  // sentence says `No`. A wording test that false-fails on correct copy gets
  // deleted rather than fixed, so the guard is the negation FORM, not a word
  // list, and `claimsIdentitiesHidden` is exercised in both directions below.
  test("no sentence claims identities are hidden", () => {
    const hits: string[] = [];
    for (const s of TIER) {
      for (const line of s.text.split("\n")) if (claimsIdentitiesHidden(line)) hits.push(`${s.rel}: ${line.trim()}`);
    }
    expect(hits).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("...and that detector CATCHES a real violation (verified by breaking it)", () => {
    expect(claimsIdentitiesHidden("Confidential MPT hides identities from the network.")).toBe(true);
    expect(claimsIdentitiesHidden("This hides who transacts with whom.")).toBe(true);
  });

  test("...and does NOT fire on the negations the tier actually renders", () => {
    expect(claimsIdentitiesHidden("No key source hides identities. Sender and receiver are public.")).toBe(false);
    expect(claimsIdentitiesHidden("It does not hide who transacts.")).toBe(false);
    expect(claimsIdentitiesHidden("Nothing here hides the sender.")).toBe(false);
  });

  test("the observer view enumerates what is public before what is hidden", () => {
    const obs = readFileSync(join(REPO, "web/api/observer.ts"), "utf8");
    expect(obs.indexOf("whatIsPublic")).toBeLessThan(obs.indexOf("whatIsHidden"));
  });
});

describe("F-1 — a zero confidential balance is publicly known", () => {
  test("the observer view says so in the ciphertext note, not in a footnote", () => {
    expect(CANONICAL_ZERO_NOTE).toMatch(/publicly known to be exactly zero/i);
    expect(CANONICAL_ZERO_NOTE).toMatch(/F-1/);
  });

  test("no sentence presents a canonically-zero balance as hidden", () => {
    expect(assertsHidden(CANONICAL_ZERO_NOTE)).toBe(false);
    expect(CANONICAL_ZERO_NOTE).toMatch(/not hidden|publicly known/i);
  });

  test("...and that detector CATCHES a note that claims the zero balance is hidden", () => {
    expect(assertsHidden('A zero balance is hidden from observers.')).toBe(true);
    expect(assertsHidden('The amount remains confidential.')).toBe(true);
    expect(assertsHidden('A zero confidential balance is not hidden.')).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("E-211 — a non-canonical ciphertext is NOT evidence of a non-zero balance", () => {
  // ⚠⚠ This test exists because the sentence it forbids was SHIPPED. Measured
  // on Devnet 2026-08-28: an account decrypting to 0 through the issuer mirror
  // carried a spending ciphertext that did not match the canonical EncZero, and
  // the page called it "Non-zero". `tools/observer-harness.ts:277` had the
  // correct hedge — "some non-zero value, or never reset" — one import away.
  //
  // ⚠ It asserts on the exported VALUES, not on the file's source text. The
  // first version scanned the source and failed on the COMMENT that documents
  // this very bug — a detector that reads comments fires on the documentation
  // of the error it is looking for (E-182's shape, in a test rather than a gate).

  test("the non-matching note does not assert the balance is non-zero", () => {
    expect(assertsNonZero(NOT_CANONICAL_NOTE)).toBe(false);
  });

  test("it says explicitly that a spent-to-zero balance looks the same", () => {
    expect(NOT_CANONICAL_NOTE).toMatch(/NOT the same as saying it is non-zero/i);
    expect(NOT_CANONICAL_NOTE).toMatch(/reached zero by spending/i);
  });

  test("the canonical-zero note still states F-1 plainly", () => {
    expect(CANONICAL_ZERO_NOTE).toMatch(/publicly known to be exactly zero/i);
    expect(assertsHidden(CANONICAL_ZERO_NOTE)).toBe(false);
  });

  test("the detector CATCHES the sentence that was actually shipped", () => {
    expect(assertsNonZero("Non-zero, and the amount is hidden from an observer.")).toBe(true);
    expect(assertsNonZero("This balance is non-zero.")).toBe(true);
  });

  test("...and does NOT fire on the corrected hedge, or on the harness's wording", () => {
    expect(assertsNonZero("That is NOT the same as saying it is non-zero.")).toBe(false);
    expect(assertsNonZero("not the canonical zero (some non-zero value, or never reset)")).toBe(false);
  });

  test("what is PUBLIC carries F-1's condition rather than claiming zeros are always visible", () => {
    const f1 = WHAT_IS_PUBLIC.filter((l) => /zero/i.test(l));
    expect(f1.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    for (const line of f1) expect(line).toMatch(/canonical/i);
  });

  test("what is HIDDEN does not describe the hidden value as non-zero", () => {
    for (const line of WHAT_IS_HIDDEN) expect(assertsNonZero(line)).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("the issuer view holds NO key and performs NO decryption", () => {
  // ⚠⚠ It DID hold one, and decrypted per request, which is a decryption
  // oracle over an unauthenticated GET — the fourth rotation trigger ADR-0003
  // names, written by the same session one file over (CLAIMS.md E-212).
  // Architecture §6 step 8 lets this tier touch the TOOL'S OUTPUT and never a
  // private key. These tests are what stop it drifting back.
  // ⚠ **The gate's own instruments, imported rather than re-derived.** These
  // needles are IDENTIFIERS, so string literals are blanked: declaring
  // `FORBIDDEN_SECRET_ENV = "WCONF_ELGAMAL_SK"` is the name being forbidden,
  // not a use of it, and a weaker stripper in the test would disagree with the
  // gate about the same file. One instrument, two callers (CLAIMS.md E-207).
  const src = readFileSync(join(REPO, "web/api/issuer.ts"), "utf8");
  const code = stripStringLiterals(stripComments(src));

  test("it never reads the issuer secret from the environment", () => {
    expect(code).not.toContain(`process.env.${FORBIDDEN_SECRET_ENV}`);
    expect(code).not.toMatch(/process\.env\[/);
  });

  test("no file under web/ reads the issuer secret", () => {
    const hits = TIER.filter((f) =>
      stripStringLiterals(stripComments(f.text)).includes(`process.env.${FORBIDDEN_SECRET_ENV}`),
    ).map((f) => f.rel);
    expect(hits).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("it spawns nothing — argv is world-readable via `ps`", () => {
    // ⚠ The version that decrypted used `decryptInRange`, which spawns
    // `mptool decrypt <ciphertext> <sk> …`. That is the exact exposure the
    // issuer CLI refuses a `--key` flag to avoid.
    // ⚠ Built from the gate's own needle list rather than re-spelled here.
    // Two reasons: one source of truth, and a literal spelling in a test file
    // is itself a secret reference the gate must then flag — which it did.
    for (const needle of SECRET_NEEDLES) expect(code).not.toContain(needle);
  });

  test("it never accepts a key from the request", () => {
    expect(code).not.toMatch(/params\.(key|sk|secret)/);
    expect(code).not.toMatch(/query\.(key|sk|secret)/);
    expect(code).not.toMatch(/headers\.get\(["'`](x-)?(key|sk|secret)/i);
  });

  // ⚠⚠ **THE FALLBACK COPY WAS STALE AND CONTRADICTED THE SAME SITE.** Before an
  // account is picked, `view` is null and the issuer page rendered a default
  // string saying the web process reads the key from its environment — false
  // since the snapshot design, and contradicting `/api/meta`'s
  // `holdsKeys: false` two clicks away. `/api-doc` carried the same sentence.
  // ⚠ **A default rendered only in an empty state is exactly where a stale
  // sentence survives**: nobody screenshots the empty state.
  test("no rendered copy claims THIS process reads the issuer key", () => {
    const hits: string[] = [];
    for (const f of TIER) {
      if (!f.rel.startsWith("web/app/")) continue;
      for (const line of f.text.split("\n")) {
        if (/^\s*(\/\/|\*|\{\/\*)/.test(line)) continue;          // a comment about the defect is not the defect
        if (/(issuer )?key is read from|key from the environment|environment only/i.test(line)) {
          hits.push(`${f.rel}: ${line.trim().slice(0, 110)}`);
        }
      }
    }
    expect(hits).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("...and the detector CATCHES the sentence that was actually rendered", () => {
    const bad = '    "The issuer key is read from this process environment and from nowhere else."';
    expect(/(issuer )?key is read from|key from the environment|environment only/i.test(bad)).toBe(true);
  });

  test("the key policy states the absence, not a guard around a presence", () => {
    expect(ISSUER_KEY_POLICY).toMatch(/holds NO issuer key/i);
    // ⚠ Was `/no oracle to authenticate/`. E-241 made the property STRONGER —
    // the tier no longer serves the decryption RESULT either — so the test
    // follows the property rather than the old sentence. Retargeted, not
    // deleted: it still fails if the policy starts describing a guard.
    expect(ISSUER_KEY_POLICY).toMatch(/no request that reaches a decryption and none that returns one/i);
    expect(ISSUER_KEY_POLICY).not.toMatch(/authenticat(e|ed|ion) (the|this) (request|caller|endpoint)/i);
  });

  // ⚠ E-241: the policy must state the WITHHOLDING, because a reader who sees
  // "no key here" may still assume the figure is served.
  test("the key policy says the decrypted figure is NOT served", () => {
    expect(ISSUER_KEY_POLICY).toMatch(/DOES NOT SERVE a decrypted balance/i);
    expect(ISSUER_KEY_POLICY).toMatch(/loopback is not uid-scoped/i);
  });

  test("it names the mirror, never a holder-keyed balance", () => {
    expect(MIRROR_FIELD_LEDGER_NAME).toBe("IssuerEncryptedBalance");
    expect(MIRROR_FIELD_LEDGER_NAME).not.toMatch(/ConfidentialBalance/);
  });

  // ⚠⚠ **THIS TEST FALSE-PASSED, AND IT WAS WRITTEN IN THE ROUND THAT FIXED A
  // FALSE PASS.** `SNAPSHOT_PATH` was a module-level `const`, bound at import
  // time, so setting the env var afterwards did nothing and `await import()`
  // returned the cached module. It read the DEFAULT path — absent in a clean
  // checkout — so `issuerView` said unavailable for that reason and the test
  // passed with the refusal DELETED. **Measured: removing both refusal lines
  // left all 46 tests green.** The path is read lazily now, and the control
  // below is what proves the assertion can fail (`CLAIMS.md` E-215).
  const withSnapshot = (body: unknown, fn: () => void) => {
    const tmp = join(REPO, `web/api/.test-snapshot-${Math.abs(hashOf(JSON.stringify(body)))}.json`);
    writeFileSync(tmp, JSON.stringify(body));
    const prev = process.env.WCONF_ISSUER_SNAPSHOT;
    process.env.WCONF_ISSUER_SNAPSHOT = tmp;
    try { fn(); } finally {
      if (prev === undefined) delete process.env.WCONF_ISSUER_SNAPSHOT;
      else process.env.WCONF_ISSUER_SNAPSHOT = prev;
      rmSync(tmp, { force: true });
    }
  };

  test("CONTROL — a clean snapshot IS read, so the refusal test below can fail", () => {
    // ⚠ Without this the refusal test proves nothing: an unavailable result is
    // the default for a missing file, which is what made it false-pass.
    withSnapshot({ producedAtUnix: 1, entries: { "a/b": { available: true, decrypted: "5" } } }, () => {
      const v = issuerView("a", "b");
      expect(v.available).toBe(true);
      // ⚠ E-241: the snapshot HAS the value; the API reports only that it exists.
      expect(v.decryptable).toBe(true);
    });
  });

  // ⚠⚠ **THE POINT OF E-241, AND THE ONLY TEST THAT FAILS IF IT REGRESSES.**
  // The decrypted figure must never cross this boundary. Loopback is not
  // uid-scoped, so a served value reaches every local user out of a file the
  // producing tool writes `mode 0600` (REVIEW-036 U1, E-228).
  test("the decrypted balance is NEVER served, even when the snapshot has it", () => {
    const secret = "123456789";
    withSnapshot({ producedAtUnix: 1, entries: { "a/b": { available: true, decrypted: secret, publicAmount: "7" } } }, () => {
      const v = issuerView("a", "b");
      expect(v.available).toBe(true);
      expect(v.decryptedWithheld).toBe(true);
      // The figure appears NOWHERE in the serialised response.
      expect(JSON.stringify(v)).not.toContain(secret);
      // ...while the public plaintext amount, which IS public, still does.
      expect(JSON.stringify(v)).toContain("7");
    });
  });

  test("CONTROL — the withholding is not vacuous: an absent value is distinguishable", () => {
    withSnapshot({ producedAtUnix: 1, entries: { "a/b": { available: true, publicAmount: "7" } } }, () => {
      expect(issuerView("a", "b").decryptable).toBe(false);
    });
  });

  test("the snapshot reader REFUSES a file carrying anything key-shaped", () => {
    withSnapshot(
      { producedAtUnix: 1, sk: "deadbeef", entries: { "a/b": { available: true, decrypted: "5" } } },
      () => expect(issuerView("a", "b").available).toBe(false),
    );
  });

  test("...and refuses one naming the secret env var anywhere in it", () => {
    withSnapshot(
      { producedAtUnix: 1, note: `produced with ${FORBIDDEN_SECRET_ENV}`, entries: { "a/b": { available: true, decrypted: "5" } } },
      () => expect(issuerView("a", "b").available).toBe(false),
    );
  });

  test("balances are DECIMAL STRINGS, so a UINT64 above 2^53 survives", () => {
    // ⚠ 18446744073709551615 is UINT64 max; Number() would render it as
    // 18446744073709552000 with no indication anything happened (E-215).
    const big = "18446744073709551615";
    withSnapshot({ producedAtUnix: 1, entries: { "a/b": { available: true, decrypted: big, publicAmount: big } } }, () => {
      const v = issuerView("a", "b");
      // ⚠ `decrypted` is withheld now (E-241), so the UINT64 property is
      // asserted on `publicAmount` — which IS public ledger data and is served.
      expect(v.publicAmount).toBe(big);
      expect(String(Number(big))).not.toBe(big); // the loss this avoids, demonstrated
    });
  });

 succeeded in 0ms:
⚠ **A second local user who cannot `connect()` the `0600` socket and cannot `cat` the `0600` snapshot can `curl` both through this tier.**

⚠⚠ **The obvious rebuttal fails.** Architecture §3 concedes defeat to *"an adversary who has code execution"* — **as the holder**. The party this tier newly serves is **strictly weaker**: a different local uid, no code execution as the holder. **§3's concession does not cover them, and `ipc.rs`'s own comment is the project's evidence that it draws the line exactly there.**

⚠⚠ **This is trigger 4's lesson applied to the KEY and not to the RESULT.** E-212's correction reads *"the trigger was written about the key ARRIVING; the oracle is the RESULT LEAVING."* The remedy moved the key out and **left the result leaving**, over the same unauthenticated GET, to the same callers. **Trigger 4 is satisfied to the letter — the decryption now happens ahead of time — and the property it was protecting is not.** `CLAIMS.md` **E-228**.

---

## Alternatives considered

### A signing web tier over a localhost HTTP bridge — rejected, and previously

An origin allowlist plus a session token. ⚠ **Withdrawn by architecture §3 rule 3 on `REVIEW-003b`'s finding**: an allowlist constrains pages, not processes; any local process forges an `Origin` header; and the issue #1 ruling puts a hostile same-host process in scope. **A value-shaped interface plus a leaked token is a spend oracle.** Recording it here so that a later session finds the rejection rather than rediscovering the design.

### Keys and proving in the browser (ADR-0001 Option 2) — rejected

⚠ **And the reason is not cost.** `CLAIMS.md` **E-53**: Option 2 is the *cheapest* option — three published npm packages, no patching, no vendoring, no build step — while Option 3 is the most expensive. **Option 3 was chosen on risk**, and `REVIEW-013c`'s two legs, handed the strongest arguments against it, both ruled Option 3 on risk alone. ⚠ **The keygen ruling additionally removes Option 2's escape hatch**: the page can no longer delegate signing and hold only an ElGamal key, because the derivation input is the master seed — so the design **welds a rotatable exposure to an unrotatable one**.

### A native shell that opens the socket — deferred, not rejected

See trigger 3. Defensible on the transport property; out of scope; an ADR if it is wanted.

### No web tier at all — rejected by the owner

The CLI demonstrates the protocol to someone who will read Rust. **The capability matrix — what each key source can and cannot do, and why — is the thing a capital-markets reader needs**, and it does not survive being explained in a terminal transcript.

---

## Deferred deliberately — recorded so they are not rediscovered as oversights

⚠ **Both were scoped, both were reachable, and both were left unbuilt on
purpose.** Recording the reasoning is the point: an unbuilt thing with no record
reads as a thing nobody thought of, and the next session rebuilds the argument
from scratch or, worse, builds the thing.

### Wallet connect — deferred (2026-08-28)

**What exists:** the wallet page states the three structural reasons a browser
wallet cannot hold a confidential position. **What does not:** any actual
connection to Xaman, GemWallet or Crossmark.

**Why deferred, and the first reason is the strongest:**

1. ⚠ **The argument does not need it.** The three reasons are structural — the
   operation needs the ElGamal secret and the account key; the ElGamal secret is
   derived from the master seed; a wallet exists in order not to release seed
   material. **A connected wallet would not make any of them more true**, and a
   demonstration that *needs* the connection to make its point has a weaker
   point.
2. **It can only demonstrate the half that already works.** A connected wallet
   proves account control and then shows that account's **observer view** —

# Custody and confidential positions — what the protocol requires of a key holder

- **Date:** 2026-08-28
- **Status:** Research. **Not adversarially reviewed.** No ruling depends on it.
- **Context:** architecture §6 step 8, decision D4. The project owner asked for a research document **and** a custody-shaped demo mode.
- **Scope:** what W-CONF's own construction obliges of anything holding a key, and what that implies for custodial models generally.

---

## ⚠ What this document does NOT have, stated first

**This repository holds no Metaco Harmonize primary sources, and none were substituted.**

**P-12's search, recorded:** `grep -rli "harmonize\|metaco"` over every `.md`, `.ts`, `.rs` and `.json` outside `node_modules`, 2026-08-28, matches **three** files — the session handover, `ADR-0003`, and architecture §6 step 8. **All three are this project naming the deliverable. None is a Harmonize document.**

So every Harmonize-specific question — which signing schemes it offers, whether its policy engine can be extended, what its approval workflow can read — is a **named gap** here rather than an answer. `CLAUDE.md`: *a named gap is a correct output; a substituted source is a corrupted one.*

**What this document does instead:** derive from *our* side what the protocol requires of a key holder, and test custodial models against that. Those requirements are properties of XLS-0096 and of this project's ruled key derivation, so they hold against **any** custody platform, named or not. That is a narrower claim than a Harmonize assessment and it is the one the evidence supports.

---

## Finding 1 — the ruled key derivation is incompatible with custodial key management

**The chain, each link in this repository:**

1. A confidential operation requires the **ElGamal secret** — to decrypt the balance being spent and to produce the proof — in addition to the XRPL account key that signs.
2. Under the ruled key generation (`docs/reviews/REVIEW-012-RULING-keygen-2026-08-18.md`, implemented in `signer/src/keygen.rs`), the ElGamal secret is **derived from the account's master family seed**.
3. A custody platform's entire purpose is **never to release seed material**. Releasing it would defeat the custody.

**Therefore a custodied account cannot derive its own viewing key.** It cannot read its own confidential balance, which is not a limitation of any integration — it follows from step 2 alone.

⚠ **The escape hatch exists and it moves the problem rather than solving it.** `KeySource::Standalone` (`signer/src/onboarding.rs:279`) is an independent ElGamal secret with its own backup, and it is what every profile written before 2026-08-20 silently was. But then **something outside the custody boundary holds a permanent decryption credential for every balance the account has ever held** — and *who holds it* is `CLAIMS.md` **E-117**, which is open and has had no adversarial review.

⚠ **E-117's axis is the honest framing, and it is sharper than a custody question:** *confidential positions, or non-custodial pooling — one or the other, today.* This project picks confidentiality because that is its premise. A design that needs *"no single party can move the float"* weighs it the other way, and ~~the comparison table in `ADR-0002` **has no row for custody at all**~~ **(struck 2026-09-13, `CLAIMS.md` E-295: the row has existed since 2026-08-20, and the same clause was struck at `:86` one round earlier without reaching this copy)**.

**What would change this:** a derivation whose input is not the master seed, or a custody platform that performs the derivation inside its own boundary and never emits either secret. **The second is not obviously impossible** — it is a key-derivation function over a seed the platform already holds — and it is the question worth putting to a custody vendor. ⚠ **It would require the derivation to be a published standard, which is issue #10, open, and no code discharges it.**

---

## Finding 2 — a policy engine cannot enforce an amount limit on a confidential amount

⚠⚠ **This is the capital-markets crux, and it is structural rather than an integration detail.**

Custodial approval workflows are written over transaction *values*: *"require two approvers above $1M"*, *"block transfers to unlisted counterparties"*, *"cap daily outflow"*. A `ConfidentialMPTSend` carries **a proof, not a value**. The amount is exactly what has been hidden, and it is hidden from *everyone* holding only public data — which includes the policy engine.

**So the first rule is unevaluable.** Not hard to implement: unevaluable, because the input does not exist in the data the engine sees.

**What survives, and it is worth being precise about:**

| policy shape | on a confidential send | why |
|---|---|---|
| *"require N approvers above amount X"* | ⚠ **unevaluable** | the amount is a proof |
| *"cap total daily outflow"* | ⚠ **unevaluable** | sums of hidden amounts are hidden |
| *"only these destinations"* | **evaluable** | the destination is public (P-4, P-11) |
| *"only during these hours"* | **evaluable** | timing is public (P-11) |
| *"only this issuance"* | **evaluable** | the issuance is public |
| *"require N approvers, unconditionally"* | **evaluable** | no amount is read |
| *"block if the account is frozen"* | **evaluable** | ledger state is public |

⚠ **The pattern: every policy over an IDENTITY, a TIME or a COUNT survives; every policy over a VALUE does not.** That is P-4 and P-11 restated as a custody constraint — this system hides amounts and hides nothing else — and it is the single most useful sentence in this document for a capital-markets reader.

**Three ways out, and none is free:**

1. **Give the policy engine the ElGamal secret.** Then it can decrypt and evaluate — and it is now a party that can read every balance, which is Finding 1's problem with a second holder added.
2. **Have the holder attest the amount alongside the proof.** The engine then enforces a policy over a *claim*, not over the transaction. ⚠ **An attestation the engine cannot verify against the proof is a policy over an honest holder's honesty**, which is not a control.
3. **Prove the bound in zero knowledge.** *"This transfer is under $1M"* is a range proof — and **XLS-0096 already carries range proofs**, so the machinery is present rather than hypothetical. Verified at source: a `ConfidentialMPTSend`'s 946-byte proof is 192 B sigma **plus a 754 B aggregated Bulletproof over two 64-bit values**, and a `ConfidentialMPTConvertBack`'s 816 B is 128 B sigma plus a **688 B single Bulletproof**; TASK ZERO records that *"the aggregated Bulletproof proves the amount lies in [0, 2⁶⁴)"* (`docs/task-zero/TASK-ZERO-2026-08-13.md`, Grade A, sizes confirmed by execution against `mpt-crypto`).

   ⚠ **What is present is a range proof over a FIXED bound — [0, 2⁶⁴), the field's own validity condition — not over a POLICY bound chosen by an approver.** Those are different proofs: one is a protocol invariant every transaction already carries, the other is a per-policy statement nobody has specified, generated by the holder, verified by the engine, and bound to the same amount the transaction moves. ⚠ **This project has neither built nor costed the second, and the gap between them is the whole question.** Recorded as a direction, not a recommendation.

---

## Finding 3 — tranche sizes are public even when the balance was not

A custody client would reasonably assume that a confidentially-held position is retired confidentially. It is not.

`MPTAmount` is a **plaintext field on every individual `ConfidentialMPTConvertBack`**, so retiring a position in tranches publishes **every tranche size** and its timing. `CLAIMS.md` **F-24**, found in this project's own facility walkthrough after that document had already passed `claims-check`, and read off two validated Devnet transactions at 95 and 191.

⚠ **For a custody client this is a reporting-surface question, not a cryptography question**, and it is the kind that surfaces after a position is opened rather than before.

---

## Finding 4 — the residual custody risk this project already carries

`CLAIMS.md` **E-117** again, in its step-7 form: the facility's Dedicated Account is **an ordinary XRPL account with an ordinary key**, so whoever holds that key can move the entire float. **Incomplete, `CLAIMS.md` E-290:** the issuer can also erase and freeze the float without that key, and the key that decrypts is also required to spend. The XLS-65 `Vault` that was rejected has a pseudo-account with **no key**, and nothing can move its assets outside the protocol's rules.

⚠ **The rejection was correct on its own grounds** — `Vault` share tokens cannot be confidential, which forces native share accounting XOR confidential investor positions — ~~**but the comparison table counts only disclosure and accounting.** It has no custody row.~~ **Struck 2026-09-13 (`CLAIMS.md` E-292): the table has had a custody row since `c34dcec` on 2026-08-20, and E-256 struck the same clause in E-117 on 2026-09-09 without reaching this copy.** This document does not reopen that decision; it records that the cost is unpriced and that a custody conversation will surface it immediately.

---

## The demo mode, and what it is

`web/app` renders a **custody-shaped key source**: a standalone ElGamal key plus an external-signer stub standing in for a custody platform, showing which flows survive and which break.

⚠⚠ **It is a SIMULATION and every surface says so.** There is no custody integration, no MPC and no HSM. `CLAIMS.md` **P-5** forbids claiming more than is delivered, and *"custody-compatible"* on a screen with a stub behind it is exactly that kind of claim. **`web/api/disclosure.test.ts` fails if any surface stops saying it**, and that test is verified by breaking it.

---

## What this document does not claim

- **That Harmonize cannot do any of this.** It makes no claim about Harmonize at all; see the opening section.
- **That the tension is unresolvable.** Finding 2's third way out — range proofs over policy bounds — is a real direction that this project has not costed.
- **That standalone keys are a solution.** They relocate Finding 1's problem to an unreviewed holder (E-117).
- **That any of this is a compliance analysis.** `CLAIMS.md` P-6: this is not a compliance project.

---

## Open, and worth putting to a custody vendor

1. Can the platform derive a secondary key from a seed **inside its boundary** and emit neither? (Finding 1's only clean exit, and it needs issue #10 closed.)
2. Can the policy engine consume a **range proof over a policy bound** rather than a value? ⚠ Note the protocol's existing Bulletproofs prove a **fixed** range, not a chosen one — the two are not the same artifact. (Finding 2's third way out.)
3. How does the platform's reporting surface handle a position whose size it cannot read? (Finding 3.)

A browser wallet cannot hold a confidential position
The three wallets examined (Xaman, GemWallet and Crossmark, on 2026-08-28) cannot, and the reasons are structural, not missing features. A wallet that kept the ElGamal key inside the extension and offered a prove-and-sign operation could; none of those examined does.
A confidential transaction needs two secrets: the ElGamal secret, to decrypt the balance and build the proof, and the XRPL account key, to sign. A wallet supplies only the second.
Under the ruled key generation, the ElGamal secret is derived from the master seed. A derived-key account has no other way to get it.
A wallet extension exists in order not to release seed material. That is the product, not a gap in its API.
So a page cannot assemble the transaction through these wallets. They are not refusing a permission; they hold nothing they are built to give a page.

W-CONF: confidential MPT on the XRPL Devnet
Devnet snapshot · signs nothing, holds no keys · not secure, not audited, not production-ready (P-5)
W-CONF
What confidential MPT on the XRP Ledger hides, and what it does not. A research project, shown on one snapshot of the Devnet.
OverviewCapability matrixObserver viewIssuer viewWalletCustody
This is a simulation
No custody platform is integrated behind this page: no MPC, no HSM, no Harmonize. It models a key-source shape, a standalone ElGamal key plus an external signer, to show which flows survive and which break.
Two findings
1. The derived key does not work with custodial key management
The ElGamal secret is derived from the master seed, and a custody platform never releases the seed. So the account cannot derive its own ElGamal key or read its own confidential balance outside the platform. A platform that ran the derivation inside its own boundary would change that; it would need the derivation published as a standard, and it is not (issue #10).
A standalone ElGamal key gets around this, but then something outside the custody platform holds a permanent decryption key. Who that should be is an open question in this project (CLAIMS.md E-117).
2. Approval policies cannot read a confidential amount
An approval workflow that holds only public data sees a proof, not a value, so a rule like “two approvers above $1M” has nothing to check. This is structural, not an integration detail: confidentiality and amount-based approval policies pull against each other. The ways out each cost something: give the policy engine the ElGamal secret, and it becomes another party that reads every balance; accept the holder’s statement of the amount, and the policy rests on the holder’s honesty; or prove the bound in zero knowledge, which this project has neither built nor costed.
Which flows survive, and which break
Each flow lists what it needs, and the verdict is computed from what a custody-shaped key source has.
Note 1: Only with a standalone ElGamal key, held outside the custody platform (E-117).
survives: Send a public XRPL payment
breaks: Onboard with the ruled derived key

survives: Onboard with a standalone ElGamal key (note 1)
survives: Read own confidential balance (note 1)
survives: Send a confidential amount (note 1)
breaks: Send confidentially, under an amount-capped approval policy (note 1)

survives: Send confidentially, under a destination-allowlist policy (note 1)
survives: Retire a position in tranches (note 1)

Publicly known to be exactly zero. This is the canonical encryption of zero, which anyone can recompute from the holder's public key, the account and the issuance, with no secret (CLAIMS.md F-1).

W-CONF: confidential MPT on the XRPL Devnet
Devnet snapshot · signs nothing, holds no keys · not secure, not audited, not production-ready (P-5)
W-CONF
What confidential MPT on the XRP Ledger hides, and what it does not. A research project, shown on one snapshot of the Devnet.
OverviewCapability matrixObserver viewIssuer viewWalletCustody
A holder is never private from the issuer
The protocol keeps a second copy of every confidential balance, the IssuerEncryptedBalance, encrypted to the issuer’s key. The issuer can always decrypt it, and no setting turns this off (CLAIMS.md P-9).
This page shows that each copy is on the ledger. It does not show the decrypted figures: a visitor could not check them, so this project does not publish them (ADR-0004 D-H3).
Where these values come from
read from https://s.devnet.rippletest.net:51234
validated ledger 6285074 at 2026-10-21T01:32:23.419Z
network_id 2 (Devnet) rippled 3.4.1
This page shows the XRPL Devnet, a test network. Its tokens have no value, and it is reset from time to time. Each value was read from Ripple's public Devnet endpoint, at the ledger and date shown, and a lying or lagging server behind it would have made it wrong. The page does not update: it shows Devnet as it was at that ledger, not as it is now. Nothing on this page signs or submits. Do not use a value shown here to build a transaction.

/**
 * build-claims-topics.ts — topic views of `CLAIMS.md`, DERIVED.
 *
 *   bun run tools/build-claims-topics.ts            # write docs/claims/by-topic/
 *   bun run tools/build-claims-topics.ts --check    # fail if stale (the gate)
 *
 * ## Why this exists, and why it is not a split
 *
 * `docs/CLAIMS-INDEX.md` answers *"where is E-181?"*. It does not answer *"what
 * has this project learned about gates?"* — for that you need the register
 * grouped by subject, and the register is chronological.
 *
 * ⚠⚠ **THE ROWS ARE NOT MOVED, AND THAT IS A MEASURED DECISION, NOT TIMIDITY.**
 * ⚠⚠ **This paragraph quoted *"only ~20% belong to exactly one; 93 of 245 matched
 * four or more"* until `REVIEW-041`. Those numbers came from an exploratory
 * nine-topic pass over WHOLE ROWS that was then replaced by this twelve-topic
 * headline classifier, and three different figures were published for the same
 * measurement before anyone noticed the PREDICATE was never stated.** The run
 * output prints the distribution, with its predicate, derived where it is
 * computed. **About half the rows carry more than one topic.** E-203 is
 * a gate that false-passed *and* a miscount *and* a review finding *and* a
 * lesson about stripping string literals. **A physical split files such a row
 * under one topic and hides it from readers of the other three.** A generated
 * view lists it under all of them.
 *
 * Three further properties a move would cost, all measured on the register:
 *
 *   - **63% of rows cite another row**, 476 cross-references in total. Moving
 *     rows scatters those across files.
 *   - **Chronology is load-bearing.** *"Seventh instance of a wrong count"* is
 *     only legible because the register is append-only and in order.
 *   - Every gate that opens `CLAIMS.md` by path would need updating and
 *     **re-verifying by breaking it**. None needs to change here.
 *
 * ## How a row gets its topics
 *
 * A **lexical rule over the row's HEADLINE** — the leading bold run of the claim
 * cell — plus an explicit `OVERRIDES` list for rows the rules do not reach.
 *
 * ⚠ **The headline, not the whole row, and that is the instrument.** Matching
 * the full row put 80% of rows in 4+ topics, because an evidence cell mentions
 * everything: the gate, the review, the Devnet run and the secret. The headline
 * states what the row is *about*.
 *
 * ⚠⚠ **What this does NOT say.** A topic is a finding aid, not a judgement. It
 * does not say a row is true, that its grade is deserved, or that the topic set
 * is the right one. It is **LEXICAL, over a NAMED SET of patterns**, and a row
 * whose headline uses different vocabulary lands only where `OVERRIDES` puts it.
 * **The row is the authority — never cite a topic file.**
 */

interface Entry { id: string; line: number; section: string; headline: string; grade: string; topics: string[] }

/**
 * The row's headline: the leading bold run of the claim cell, else its opening.
 *
 * ⚠ This is what the rules see. A row whose claim opens with unbolded prose
 * falls back to its first 200 characters, which is why `OVERRIDES` exists.
 */
/** A bold lead shorter than this says nothing on its own — see below. */
const MIN_HEADLINE = 40;

/**
 * The row's headline: the leading bold run of the claim cell, else its opening.
 *
 * ⚠⚠ **A NON-GREEDY FIRST BOLD RUN CAN THROW THE ROW AWAY.** `E-17` opens
 * `**When set**, \`sfDomainID\` on the \`MPTokenIssuance\` gates confidential
 * transfers…`, so this returned **`"When set"`** — nine characters carrying no
 * subject. It matched no topic, and the first repair was an `OVERRIDES` entry,
 * which asserts *the patterns do not reach this row* when the truth was *the
 * extractor discarded the row* (REVIEW-040 M5).
 *
 * A bold lead shorter than `MIN_HEADLINE` is treated as an opening clause
 * rather than a headline, and the surrounding text is taken instead.
 */
export function headline(claim: string): string {
  const flat = claim.replace(/⚠+/g, "").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
  const bold = flat.match(/^\*\*(.+?)\*\*/);
  if (bold && bold[1].length >= MIN_HEADLINE) return bold[1];
  // Strip emphasis markers so a short lead and its continuation read as one.
  return flat.replace(/\*\*/g, "").slice(0, 200);
}

export function byRules(head: string): string[] {
  return TOPICS.filter((t) => t.pattern.test(head)).map((t) => t.slug);
}

export function classify(id: string, head: string): string[] {
  const hits = byRules(head);
  for (const extra of OVERRIDES[id] ?? []) if (!hits.includes(extra)) hits.push(extra);
  return hits;
}

export function parse(text: string): Entry[] {
  const out: Entry[] = [];
  let section = "(none)";
  const lines = text.split("\n");
  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
    const h = lines[i].match(/^## (.+)$/);
    if (h) { section = h[1].replace(/[*`]/g, "").trim(); continue; }
    const m = lines[i].match(ROW);
    if (!m) continue;
    // ⚠ The SHARED splitter, so this file and the gate cut cells the same way.
    // ⚠⚠ This comment used to say *"a pipe inside a code span is content"*. It is
    // NOT — GFM splits on it, and that false belief cost five live rows
    // (REVIEW-041). Only `\|` is content (REVIEW-042).
    const cells = contentCells(lines[i]).map((c) => c.trim());
    const claim = cells[1] ?? "";
    const head = headline(claim);
    out.push({
      id: m[1], line: i + 1, section, headline: head,
      grade: summarise(cells.length >= 3 ? (cells[cells.length - 1] ?? "") : "", 22) || "—",
      topics: classify(m[1], head),
    });
  }
  return out;
}

function renderTopic(t: Topic, rows: Entry[]): string {
  const L = [
    `# ${t.title}`,
    "",
    "⚠⚠ **GENERATED. DO NOT HAND-EDIT.** Rebuild with `bun run tools/build-claims-topics.ts`;",
    "`make check-claims-topics` fails if this file drifts from `CLAIMS.md`.",
    "",
    t.blurb,
    "",
    "⚠ **A row may appear under several topics, and that is deliberate** — filing each",
    "row under exactly one would hide it from readers of the others. **The row in",
    "[`CLAIMS.md`](../../../CLAIMS.md) is the authority; never cite this file.**",
    "",
    "⚠⚠ **THIS INDEXES HEADLINES, NOT ROW BODIES.** A topic is assigned by matching the",
    "row's opening headline. **A point discussed only inside a row's evidence prose is",
    "invisible here** — a reader in `REVIEW-040` put their confidence at ~60% for *\"everything",
    "about secrets\"* and said they would fall back to grep. **They were right to.** For an",
    "exhaustive sweep, search `CLAIMS.md` directly.",
    "",
    `**${rows.length} rows.**`,
    "",
    "| id | section | headline | grade |",
    "|---|---|---|---|",
  ];
  for (const e of rows) {
    L.push(`| [${e.id}](../../../CLAIMS.md#L${e.line}) | ${shortSection(e.section)} | ${summarise(e.headline, 150)} | ${e.grade} |`);
  }
  L.push("");
  return L.join("\n");
}

function shortSection(s: string): string {
  return s.split("—")[0].trim().replace("Standing prohibitions", "Prohibitions")
    .replace("Findings", "Findings").replace("Pending", "Pending") || "—";
}

function renderReadme(entries: Entry[], byTopic: Map<string, Entry[]>): string {
  const L = [
    "# CLAIMS by topic",
    "",
    "⚠⚠ **GENERATED. DO NOT HAND-EDIT.** Rebuild with `bun run tools/build-claims-topics.ts`;",
    "`make check-claims-topics` fails if these files drift from `CLAIMS.md`.",
    "",
    "[`CLAIMS.md`](../../../CLAIMS.md) is chronological and append-only. **These are views of",
    "it grouped by subject** — the rows are not moved, and a row appears under every topic",
    "it belongs to. [`docs/CLAIMS-INDEX.md`](../../CLAIMS-INDEX.md) answers *where is E-181*;",
    "these answer *what has this project learned about X*.",
    "",
    `**${entries.length} rows across ${byTopic.size} topics**, counted where they are parsed.`,
    "⚠ The topic counts below sum to more than the row count, because a row can carry",
    "several topics. That is the point of a view rather than a split.",
    "",
    "| topic | rows | what is in it |",
    "|---|---|---|",
  ];
  for (const t of TOPICS) {
    const rows = byTopic.get(t.slug) ?? [];
    L.push(`| [${t.title}](${t.slug}.md) | ${rows.length} | ${t.blurb} |`);
  }
  L.push("", "⚠ **A topic is a finding aid, not a judgement.** It says nothing about whether a",
    "row is true or its grade deserved. Assignment is **LEXICAL, over a NAMED SET** of",
    "patterns matched against each row's headline, plus an explicit override list in",
    "`tools/build-claims-topics.ts` for the rows the patterns do not reach.",
    "",
    "⚠⚠ **WHAT THESE VIEWS DO NOT DO** (`REVIEW-040`):",
    "",
    "- **They index HEADLINES, not row bodies.** A point made only inside a row's evidence",
    "  prose is invisible to every file here. **Grep `CLAIMS.md` for an exhaustive sweep.**",
    `- **\`protocol-and-crypto\` holds ${(byTopic.get("protocol-and-crypto") ?? []).length} of ${entries.length} rows.** A filter returning that share of the`,
    "  corpus has not narrowed much. It is disclosed rather than re-cut, because re-cutting",
    "  the taxonomy would invalidate the measurements this round was reviewed against.",
    "- **A row's topics are as good as its headline.** A row whose headline uses different",
    "  vocabulary lands only where the override list puts it.", "");
  return L.join("\n");
}

const text = readFileSync(SRC, "utf8");
const entries = parse(text);
if (entries.length === 0) {
  console.log("FAIL: parsed ZERO rows from CLAIMS.md — the topic views would be empty.");
  process.exit(1);
}

// --- completeness and staleness, before anything is written ----------------
const ids = new Set(entries.map((e) => e.id));
const slugs = new Set(TOPICS.map((t) => t.slug));
const problems: string[] = [];
for (const [id, ts] of Object.entries(OVERRIDES)) {
  if (!ids.has(id)) problems.push(`OVERRIDES names ${id}, which CLAIMS.md does not contain`);
  for (const t of ts) if (!slugs.has(t)) problems.push(`OVERRIDES[${id}] names unknown topic "${t}"`);
}
/**
 * ⚠⚠ **A REDUNDANT OVERRIDE IS A FALSE STATEMENT ABOUT THE RULES, AND ELEVEN OF
 * THE FIRST THIRTY-SEVEN BECAME ONE WITHIN AN HOUR.** Each entry asserts *the
 * patterns do not reach this row*. Widening a pattern can make that untrue, and
 * nothing would say so — the file would keep a hand-maintained list that no
 * longer does anything, which is the rot this project has recorded seventeen
 * times. **Deleting the line is the whole fix.**
 */
for (const [id, ts] of Object.entries(OVERRIDES)) {
  const e = entries.find((x) => x.id === id);
  if (!e) continue; // already reported above as naming a row that does not exist
  const rules = new Set(byRules(e.headline));
  if (ts.length === 0) {
    problems.push(`OVERRIDES[${id}] is EMPTY — it adds nothing. Delete the line.`);
    continue;
  }
  // ⚠⚠ **PER MEMBER, NOT PER ENTRY.** This used `ts.every(...)`, so an override
  // was flagged only when EVERY topic it named had become rule-covered. A
  // partially redundant entry — `E-111` naming `decisions-and-scope`, which its
  // "ADR-0002's second round…" headline already matches — sat undetected on the
  // clean tree (REVIEW-040 M4, mechanism from leg A, live instance from leg B).
  const dead = ts.filter((t) => rules.has(t));
  if (dead.length) {
    problems.push(
      `OVERRIDES[${id}] names ${dead.length} topic(s) the patterns ALREADY give it: ` +
        `${dead.join(", ")}. Remove ${dead.length === ts.length ? "the line" : "those entries"}.`,
    );
  }
}

const orphans = entries.filter((e) => e.topics.length === 0);
for (const o of orphans) problems.push(`${o.id} matches no topic — add a pattern or an OVERRIDES entry: ${o.headline.slice(0, 60)}`);
if (problems.length) {
  console.log(`FAIL: ${problems.length} problem(s) — every row must carry at least one topic.`);
  for (const p of problems) console.log(`  ${p}`);
  process.exit(1);
}

const byTopic = new Map<string, Entry[]>();
for (const t of TOPICS) byTopic.set(t.slug, []);
for (const e of entries) for (const t of e.topics) byTopic.get(t)!.push(e);

const files = new Map<string, string>();
files.set("README.md", renderReadme(entries, byTopic));
for (const t of TOPICS) files.set(`${t.slug}.md`, renderTopic(t, byTopic.get(t.slug)!));

if (process.argv.includes("--check")) {
  let stale: string[] = [];
  let present: string[] = [];
  try { present = readdirSync(OUTDIR).filter((f) => f.endsWith(".md")); } catch { /* absent */ }
  for (const [name, body] of files) {
    let cur = "";
    try { cur = readFileSync(join(OUTDIR, name), "utf8"); } catch { /* absent */ }
    if (cur !== body) stale.push(name);
  }
  // ⚠ A file left behind by a REMOVED topic is drift too, and byte-comparing
  // only the files we generate would never see it.
  for (const f of present) if (!files.has(f)) stale.push(`${f} (orphaned — no topic generates it)`);
  if (stale.length) {
    console.log(`FAIL: ${stale.length} topic file(s) STALE or orphaned: ${stale.join(", ")}`);
    console.log("      Rebuild them:  bun run tools/build-claims-topics.ts");
    process.exit(1);
  }
  console.log(`PASS: ${files.size} topic files match CLAIMS.md — ${entries.length} rows, every row carrying`);
  console.log(`      at least one of ${TOPICS.length} topics, regenerated and byte-compared.`);
  console.log("⚠ LEXICAL, over a NAMED SET of headline patterns plus an override list. It says");
  console.log("  the views are CURRENT — nothing about whether a row is true or well filed.");
} else {
  mkdirSync(OUTDIR, { recursive: true });
  for (const [name, body] of files) writeFileSync(join(OUTDIR, name), body);
  console.log(`wrote ${files.size} files to docs/claims/by-topic/ — ${entries.length} rows`);
  // ⚠⚠ **THE DISTRIBUTION IS PRINTED, NOT RESTATED.** Three different numbers
  // were given for "how many rows are single-topic" across two review rounds —
  // 113, 119 and 121 — and all three were right for a DIFFERENT predicate
  // (rules-only vs final assignment; which cohort; which commit). **A bare
  // number here is meaningless without its predicate** (`CLAIMS.md` E-236), so
  // the predicate is stated and the figure is computed where it is printed.
  const dist = new Map<number, number>();
  for (const e of entries) dist.set(e.topics.length, (dist.get(e.topics.length) ?? 0) + 1);
  const one = dist.get(1) ?? 0;
  const fourPlus = [...dist].filter(([k]) => k >= 4).reduce((n, [, v]) => n + v, 0);
  console.log(
    `\n  Topics per row — FINAL assignment (rules + overrides), ALL sections, this tree:`,
  );
  console.log(
    `    ${[...dist].sort((a, b) => a[0] - b[0]).map(([k, v]) => `${k}:${v}`).join("  ")}`,
  );
  console.log(
    `    exactly one topic: ${one} of ${entries.length} ` +
      `(${((100 * one) / entries.length).toFixed(1)}%)   four or more: ${fourPlus}`,
  );
  console.log(
    `  ⚠ The MULTI-topic rows — ${entries.length - one} of ${entries.length} ` +
      `(${((100 * (entries.length - one)) / entries.length).toFixed(1)}%) — are what a SPLIT` +
      `\n    would force into a single home. This line used to point at the SINGLETON` +
      `\n    share, which is the other side of the split (REVIEW-042). It is` +
      `\n    the number the design decision rests on, and it is derived here rather` +
      `\n    than quoted, because three different figures were published for it.`,
  );
  for (const t of TOPICS) console.log(`  ${String(byTopic.get(t.slug)!.length).padStart(4)}  ${t.slug}`);
}

/**
 * Where a hosted page's ledger values came from, and the accepted risk wording.
 *
 * ⚠ **Every hosted page that renders a ledger value renders this**, and the
 * hosted gate checks it from the built HTML: the D-H2 wording, the network
 * check and the ledger index (`ADR-0004`, "What phase 2 step 4's gate must
 * check"). The `data-` attributes are what the gate reads.
 */
import { Panel } from "../components/Verdict";
import { SNAPSHOT } from "./data";
import { DH2_WORDING } from "./wording";

export function LedgerReading() {
  const s = SNAPSHOT.source;
  return (
    <Panel title="Where these values come from" tone="warn">
      <div className="text-sm space-y-1" data-ledger-source="" data-network-id={s.networkId} data-ledger-index={s.ledgerIndex}>
        <div><span className="opacity-60">read from</span> <code>{s.endpoint}</code></div>
        <div>
          <span className="opacity-60">validated ledger</span> <code>{s.ledgerIndex}</code>{" "}
          <span className="opacity-60">at</span> <code>{SNAPSHOT.readAt}</code>
        </div>
        <div>
          <span className="opacity-60">network_id</span> <code>{s.networkId}</code> (Devnet){" "}
          <span className="opacity-60">rippled</span> <code>{s.buildVersion}</code>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div className="mt-3 space-y-2" data-dh2-wording="">
        {DH2_WORDING.map((p) => <p key={p} className="text-sm leading-relaxed">{p}</p>)}
      </div>
    </Panel>
  );
}

/** One account's address and note, with the ledger it was read at. The panel title carries its label. */
export function AccountHeading({ address, note }: { address: string; note: string }) {
  return (
    <div className="mb-3">
      <code className="text-[10px] opacity-60 break-all" data-ledger-value="">{address}</code>
      <p className="text-xs opacity-75 mt-1">{note}</p>
      <p className="text-xs opacity-60 mt-1">read at validated ledger {SNAPSHOT.source.ledgerIndex}</p>
    </div>
  );
}

/** What the pinned ledger said when there is no position to show. */
export function AbsentReading({ state }: { state: string }) {
  const n = SNAPSHOT.source.ledgerIndex;
  const at = `At validated ledger ${n}`;
  const text: Record<string, string> = {
    // ⚠ `ADR-0004`'s own sentence, word for word (its "Devnet resets" section).
    "account-missing":
      `This account does not exist on Devnet at ledger ${n}. Devnet is reset from time to time and the demo accounts are throwaway. No other source is substituted.`,
    "issuance-missing": `${at} the demo issuance does not exist, so no account holds a position in it.`,
    "no-position": `${at} this account exists and holds no position in the demo issuance.`,
  };
  return <p className="text-sm" data-ledger-value="">{text[state] ?? `Unrecognised state ${JSON.stringify(state)}.`}</p>;
}

export const DH2_WORDING: readonly string[] = [

/** The network every hosted reading must come from. */
export const DEVNET_NETWORK_ID = 2;
/**
 * The hosted demo's one pinned snapshot: `ADR-0004`, architecture §6 step 9.
 *
 * Runs at BUILD time, inside the isolated build, and never in a visitor's
 * browser. It opens the reader the local tier already uses
 * (`facility/src/loopback.ts`) against ONE named endpoint under the named risk
 * acceptance, pins one validated ledger, and reads every value the hosted pages
 * render from it. It writes public ledger data only.
 *
 * ⚠ **A failed read stops the build.** A negative read the pinned ledger
 * answered (`entryNotFound`, carrying that ledger's index) is recorded as what it
 * is: a missing account, a missing position or a missing issuance. Nothing is
 * substituted (`CLAUDE.md`: a substituted source is a corrupted one), and no
 * failed read is rendered as an empty account (architecture §6 step 9's
 * falsifier).
 *
 * ⚠ **No issuer figure.** D-H3 was ruled A (`CLAIMS.md` E-331). The snapshot
 * records whether `IssuerEncryptedBalance` is present and the key it is under,
 * both ledger readings, and holds no key and decrypts nothing.
 *
 *   WCONF_ACCEPT_REMOTE_LEDGER_RISK="<the sentence>" WCONF_HOSTED_COMMIT=<sha> \
 *   WCONF_HOSTED_CANONICAL_URL=https://<name>.vercel.app bun run web/hosted/snapshot.ts <out.json>
 */

import { writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { LoopbackLedger, LedgerRefusal } from "../../facility/src/loopback.ts";
import { viewOf } from "../api/observer.ts";
import { DEMO_ACCOUNTS, DEMO_ISSUANCE, validDemoAccounts } from "../api/demo-accounts.ts";
import { CAPABILITY_MATRIX, INVARIANTS, MASTER_SEED_DISCLOSURE, DERIVATION_NOT_PUBLISHED, WALLET_CODEC_GAP } from "../api/capability.ts";
import { walkFlows } from "../api/custody-sim.ts";
import { SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA, type HostedAccount, type HostedSnapshot } from "./snapshot-types.ts";

export { SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA };
export type { HostedAccount, HostedSnapshot };

/**
 * The one ledger endpoint the hosted build may read. ⚠ A constant, not an
 * input: a second endpoint, as a fallback or otherwise, is a rotation trigger
 * (`ADR-0004` trigger 3), so no variable can name one.
 */
export const HOSTED_ENDPOINT = "https://s.devnet.rippletest.net:51234";

/** One account at the pinned ledger. Exported for tests. */
export async function readAccount(
  snap: { accountExists(a: string): Promise<boolean>; mptoken: (a: string, i: string) => Promise<any>; index: number },
  account: { address: string; issuanceId: string; label: string; note: string },
  /** The issuance as the snapshot already read it, or null for a missing one. Not read again here. */
  iss: any | null,
): Promise<HostedAccount> {
  const base = { address: account.address, label: account.label, note: account.note };
  if (!(await snap.accountExists(account.address))) {
    return { ...base, state: "account-missing", observer: null, issuerMirror: null };
  }
  if (!iss) return { ...base, state: "issuance-missing", observer: null, issuerMirror: null };
  // ⚠ One read of the position, and the view is built from it and from the
  // issuance the snapshot already read (`REVIEW-059` R1-8: both were read again).
  const mpt = await snap.mptoken(account.address, account.issuanceId);
  if (!mpt) return { ...base, state: "no-position", observer: null, issuerMirror: null };
  const observer = viewOf(account.address, account.issuanceId, mpt, iss);
  return {
    ...base,
    state: "present",
    observer,
    issuerMirror: mpt.issuerEncryptedBalance
      ? { present: true, ciphertext: mpt.issuerEncryptedBalance }
      : { present: false },
  };
}

export async function takeSnapshot(commit: string, canonicalUrl: string, endpoint = HOSTED_ENDPOINT): Promise<HostedSnapshot> {
  if (endpoint !== HOSTED_ENDPOINT) throw new Error(`the hosted build reads ${HOSTED_ENDPOINT} and nothing else (ADR-0004 trigger 3)`);
  if (!/^[0-9a-f]{40}$/.test(commit)) throw new Error(`WCONF_HOSTED_COMMIT must be a full 40-hex commit id, not ${JSON.stringify(commit)}`);
  if (!/^https:\/\/[a-z0-9.-]+\/?$/.test(canonicalUrl)) throw new Error(`WCONF_HOSTED_CANONICAL_URL must be an https origin, not ${JSON.stringify(canonicalUrl)}`);
  const accounts = validDemoAccounts();
  if (accounts.length !== DEMO_ACCOUNTS.length) throw new Error("a demo account failed its own format check; fix web/api/demo-accounts.ts");

  const ledger = await LoopbackLedger.open(endpoint);
  const snap = await ledger.snapshot();
  const readAt = new Date().toISOString();

  let issuanceExists = true;
  let iss: any = null;
  try {
    iss = await snap.issuance(DEMO_ISSUANCE);
  } catch (e) {
    if (!(e instanceof LedgerRefusal && e.code === "REFUSED_LEDGER_ENTRY_MISSING")) throw e;
    issuanceExists = false;
  }

  const out: HostedAccount[] = [];
  for (const a of accounts) out.push(await readAccount(snap, a, issuanceExists ? iss : null));

  return {
    schema: SNAPSHOT_SCHEMA,
    readAt,
    commit,
    canonicalUrl: canonicalUrl.replace(/\/$/, ""),
    source: {
      endpoint: ledger.endpoint,
      networkId: ledger.identity.networkId,
      buildVersion: ledger.identity.buildVersion,
      ledgerIndex: snap.index,
    },
    issuance: issuanceExists
      ? {
          id: DEMO_ISSUANCE,
          exists: true,
          issuer: iss.issuer,
          confidentialOutstandingAmount: iss.confidentialOutstandingAmountRaw,
          issuerEncryptionKey: iss.issuerEncryptionKey,
          hasAuditorKey: Boolean(iss.auditorEncryptionKey),
        }
      : { id: DEMO_ISSUANCE, exists: false },
    accounts: out,
    repositoryText: {
      capabilities: {
        rows: CAPABILITY_MATRIX,
        invariants: INVARIANTS,
        disclosures: { masterSeed: MASTER_SEED_DISCLOSURE, derivationNotPublished: DERIVATION_NOT_PUBLISHED },
        namedGaps: { walletCodec: WALLET_CODEC_GAP },
      },
      custody: walkFlows(),
    },
  };
}

if (import.meta.main) {
  const out = process.argv[2];
  if (!out) throw new Error("usage: bun run web/hosted/snapshot.ts <out.json>");
  const snapshot = await takeSnapshot(process.env.WCONF_HOSTED_COMMIT ?? "", process.env.WCONF_HOSTED_CANONICAL_URL ?? "");
  writeFileSync(out, JSON.stringify(snapshot, null, 2) + "\n");
  const states = snapshot.accounts.map((a) => `${a.label.split(" —")[0]}: ${a.state}`).join(", ");
  console.log(`snapshot: ledger ${snapshot.source.ledgerIndex} on ${snapshot.source.endpoint}, rippled ${snapshot.source.buildVersion}; ${states}`);
}

const EMAIL = /[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9-]+(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9-]+)*\.[A-Za-z]{2,}/g;

export function redactEmails(text: string): string {
  return text.replace(EMAIL, EMAIL_MARKER);
}

const LICENCE_FILES = ["LICENSE", "LICENSE.md", "LICENSE.txt", "license", "license.md", "LICENCE"];

/** A package root's licence file, or null. */
export function licenceFileOf(root: string): string | null {
  return LICENCE_FILES.map((f) => join(root, f)).find(existsSync) ?? null;
}

/** The notice as it is shipped: the package's licence file, emails removed, trailing space trimmed. */
export function shippedNotice(root: string): string | null {
  const f = licenceFileOf(root);
  return f ? redactEmails(readFileSync(f, "utf8")).trimEnd() : null;
}

- **R3-6 | HIGH | R2-4’s schema still accepts malformed snapshot timestamps. | Evidence:** `manifestProblems` and preflight both return `[]` for `2026-99-99T99:99:99.999Z`; the read-time case also updates the pages and verdict. `web/hosted/deploy-preflight.ts:42` checks timestamp punctuation, not calendar validity. Removing `isolation` or `environment` also passes, contradicting line 47’s “Every field the build writes is required.” **Smallest fix:** validate timestamps by parsing and exact round-trip comparison, and define the complete manifest schema—or narrow the “every field” claim.

- **R3-7 | LOW | R2-5’s charset parser can inspect a fictitious parameter inside a quoted value. | Evidence:** `bun run review-work-r3/release-probes.ts` prints:
  
  ```text
  {"type":"text/html; note=\";charset=utf-8\"; charset=utf-16le",
   "effectiveCharset":"utf-16le","result":[]}
  ```
  
  `node:util`’s `MIMEType` identifies the actual charset; comparison passes because `web/hosted/compare-deployed.ts:50` splits inside the quoted string. Correct UTF-8 aliases `utf8` and `unicode-1-1-utf-8` instead produce 17 false failures. Those labels denote UTF-8 in the [Encoding Standard](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#names-and-labels). **Smallest fix:** use a MIME parser and compare the resolved encoding.

- **R3-8 | HIGH | R2-6 retains an event gap during the newly added inspection. | Evidence:** source-supported, **browser confirmation pending**. At `web/hosted/browser-check.ts:210`, `inspect` receives an already-copied event slice. Inside `inspect`, evaluating `window.__violations.splice(0)` can emit a console error after that snapshot. Line 212 then starts the click interval after the error, excluding it from both inspections. The prepared `second-home-inspect-gap` copy logs synchronously from that operation only on the second overview load; its gate and preflight return `[]`. **Smallest fix:** consume events using a continuous cursor, including events arriving during inspection, instead of opening a new interval after inspection returns.

- **R3-9 | HIGH | R2-7’s requested clipping check is absent. | Evidence:** source-supported, **browser confirmation pending**. `web/hosted/browser-check.ts:175` measures an element’s rectangle, opacity and `checkVisibility`, without testing clipping. `[data-dh2-wording]{clip-path:inset(50%)}` removes the disclosure visually while retaining those properties and its `innerText`. Ancestor overflow clipping is similarly unchecked. Conversely, `display:contents` leaves text visible but removes the element boxes that this check requires. The [CSSOM visibility algorithm](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#dom-element-checkvisibility) does not establish freedom from clipping. **Smallest fix:** test the disclosure’s painted text regions against clipping ancestors; permit visible text hosted by elements without their own boxes.
